# Keyboard and Mouse 🖱️

#### Course: Brick Breaker with JavaScript

## Keyboard and Mouse 🖱️

The paddle needs to respond to two types of input at the same time. Keyboard and mouse. They work differently so you handle them differently.

Keyboard: state tracking.

Instead of reacting to each keypress as a one-time event, we track which keys are currently held down using an object:

```javascriptDOM
window.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
  this.keys[e.key] = true;
});

window.addEventListener("keyup", (e) => {
  this.keys[e.key] = false;
});
```

Each frame, we check that object and move the paddle if the right key is held. This gives smooth, continuous movement as long as the key stays pressed.

Mouse: position tracking with easing.

The mouse tells us where the cursor is — but instead of snapping the paddle there instantly, we move it a little closer each frame:

```javascriptDOM
this.x += ((this.mouseX - this.width / 2) - this.x) * 0.25;
```

Each frame the paddle covers 25% of the remaining distance to the target. This feels smooth and natural rather than robotic.

Choosing between the two.

Running both at the same time causes conflict — the mouse easing will constantly fight the keyboard movement. Instead, the paddle uses a control property to decide which input to listen to each frame:

```javascriptDOM
if (this.control === "keyboard") {
  // move with arrow keys
} else {
  // ease toward mouse
}
```
